newsitem.title: USA: DeBartolo pulls out of casino on NFL concerns.
newsitem.headline: DeBartolo pulls out of casino on NFL concerns.

text.p: The DeBartolo family's gambling division said Tuesday it was withdrawing from the casino part of a Louisiana resort project to avoid arousing concerns among National Football League owners about gambling.

Closely held DeBartolo Entertainment, the owner of the gambling division, also owns the San Francisco 49ers professional football team. Its Louisiana Gaming unit will retain its interest in the entertainment and retail components of the Bossier City, La., riverboat project, Cane's Landing, the company said.

A DeBartolo spokesman said the company withdrew "before it became an issue for the team owners and the NFL." NFL owners have been concerned that any potential connection with gambling might affect teams or their owners.

DeBartolo also owns a racetrack within five miles of the Cane's Landing project but the spokesman said there has not been any objection from the NFL regarding the track because of DeBartolo's limited interest in the project.
The DeBartolo company would have owned a 50 percent stake in the gambling part of the Cane's Landing project.
Hollywood Casino Corp., which is developing the project, said it will ask the Louisiana Gaming Control Board for a new partner for the project.
DeBartolo Entertainment has no corporate affiliation with the Simon DeBartolo Group Inc., a real estate investment trust founded by the same family, the spokesman said.
